jobs.title: CEO
jobs.description:
**Chief Executive Officer (CEO)**

**The Joy Culture Foundation (TJCF)** \| Menlo Park, CA \| Hybrid

The CEO is TJCF’s chief ambassador and executive leader, responsible for mission delivery, organizational health, strategic growth, and sustained community impact. In partnership with the Board, the CEO sets vision and priorities, leads a small high\-performing team (staff and volunteers), stewards major donor and partner relationships, and ensures excellent programming and library services.

**Key Responsibilities1\) Strategy \& Mission Delivery**

● Lead multi\-year strategic planning and annual operating plans that align programs and community needs while ensuring long\-term financial sustainability and legal compliance

● Deliver high\-quality and meaningful programs that advance TJCF’s vision and create lasting community impact

● Translate strategy into measurable goals, budgets, timelines, and outcomes

**2\) Organizational Leadership**

● Hire, coach, motivate, and retain a small, mission\-aligned team, including core staff, teachers, and librarians

● Champion a culture of community, kindness and teamwork

● Develop volunteer leadership pipelines; recognize and grow community champions

**3\) Board Governance** 

● Partner closely with the Board on strategy, policy, and performance; prepare timely reports and materials; run quarterly board meetings

● Support Board development: recruitment, onboarding, committee engagement, and effective meetings.

**2\) Fundraising \& Donor Relations**

● Own annual contributed\-revenue goals across major gifts, grants, events, corporate sponsorships, and community giving

● Build and manage a robust major donor pipeline; personally cultivate, solicit, and steward top prospects

● Serve as primary spokesperson; strengthen brand, marketing, and media presence

● Build partnerships with schools, libraries, civic organizations, cultural groups, and sponsors

**Qualifications**

● 10\+ years of progressive leadership in nonprofits, education, libraries, museums, community development, or startups

● Deep commitment to advancing TJCF’s mission and vision

● Inspiring leader, communicator and relationship builder

● Builder of teams, systems, and culture in resource\-conscious environments

● Strategic thinker who executes with discipline and clarity

● Strong financial acumen

● Adaptable, hands\-on, and calm under pressure—comfortable switching between high\-level strategy and day\-to\-day operations

● Bilingual Mandarin/English

● Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree a plus (MA, MPA, MBA, MLIS, or related).

**About TJCF**

The Joy Culture Foundation (TJCF) is a community\-driven nonprofit dedicated to family learning and bilingual cultural enrichment. We operate the **Little Bookworm Chinese Library** in Menlo Park and host high\-impact community programs such as the **Little Entrepreneur Fair**, seasonal cultural family days (CNY/Dragon Boat/Mid\-Autumn), reading challenges, weekend classes, and youth leadership initiatives. Our vision is a welcoming, bilingual hub where families learn, connect, and thrive.

**How to apply** 

Email CV to lulu.roberts@thejoyculturefoundation.org

Pay: From $80,000\.00 per year

Benefits:

* Flexible schedule

Work Location: Hybrid remote in Menlo Park, CA 94025

jobs.description:
**Adult Day Care Program Director**

**Bushwick Adult Day Care** is seeking a **Program Director** for our Adult Day Care in Brooklyn, New York. The Ideal candidate will have a background in ADC and be extremely organized.

**Must have Managerial Experience**

**Competitive Compensation \& comprehensive benefits package.**

 **DUTIES:**

* Perform/direct all marketing/outreach activities related to diversifying the registrant base in order to increase/maintain program census in accordance with CHC strategic plan.
* Plan, develop, organize, and implement all activities and services provided by the program.
* Ensure that established guidelines, regulations, and fiscal restraints are observed.
* Develop \& maintain administrative plans and procedures.

jobs.description:
* 559821
* New York
* School of Law
* Full Time
* Opening on: Sep 26 2026
* Grade 15
  


* Job Type: Officer of Administration
* Bargaining Unit:
* Regular/Temporary: Regular
* End Date if Temporary:
* Hours Per Week: 35
* Standard Work Schedule:
* Building:
* Salary Range: $160,000 \- $175,000

*The salary of the finalist selected for this role will be set based on a variety of factors, including but not limited to departmental budgets, qualifications, experience, education, licenses, specialty, and training. The above hiring range represents the University's good faith and reasonable estimate of the range of possible compensation at the time of posting.*  

Position Summary


Reporting to the Associate Dean of Students and Registration Services, the Executive Director and Registrar serves as the lead administrator for the Office of Registration Services (ORS) at Columbia Law School. The Registrar leads a dedicated team of higher education professionals responsible for academic policy implementation, registration operations, recordkeeping, exam administration, grade tracking, graduation clearance, and strict regulatory compliance (including ABA standards, NYS Bar requirements, and FERPA). Working closely with the Office of the Vice Dean of Academic Affairs, the Office of Student Services, the Office of Graduate Degree Programs and other Law School and University partners, the Registrar ensures data integrity across institutional databases while driving digital transformation to enhance student\-facing and administrative workflows to ensure a positive, efficient, and professional student learning experience.


Responsibilities


**Academic Operations \& Registration Management (30%)**


* Lead biannual registration, course lottery allocations, cross\-registration (including Columbia Graduate Schools such as Columbia Business School (CBS) and the School for International and Public Affairs (SIPA), and the Columbia/NYU Exchange Program)), and add/drop processes.
* Manage course setup and scheduling in partnership with the Vice Dean of Academic Affairs, overseeing classroom assignments via EMS and bulk course uploads into Columbia University’s Student Information System (SIS) and Vergil platform.
* Reconcile student enrollment data between internal systems (BORIS/LawNet) and University SIS engines to ensure complete accuracy for billing, residency tracking, and degree audits.
* Consult with University registrar’s office and law school stakeholders to draft academic year calendars, pre\-registration and add/drop calendars.
* Respond to inquiries for various reports. Ensure records are accurately transmitted to the University Registrar.

### **Compliance, Bar Admission \& External Reporting (25%)**


* Serve as the Law School’s primary authority on compliance with ABA Standards (including credit hour verification, distance learning limits, and annual questionnaire filings).
* Direct the certification process for student character, fitness, certificate of attendance, and degree completion for state bar examiners across US jurisdictions, with primary oversight of New York State Bar filings.
* Facilitate data collection and reporting for ABA Student \& Bar Passage Questionnaires and internal institutional research in coordination with other Law School units (including the Business Office and Professional Affairs).

### **Exam Administration, Grading \& Degree Clearance (20%)**


* Oversee year\-round examination administration for J.D., ELL.M., and LL.M.degree programs, ensuring full system integrity, anonymous grading protocols, and accommodation workflows in collaboration with the Office of Disability Services (ODS) and Law School disability liaisons.
* Direct the timely collection of faculty grades, grade curve enforcement, issuance of honors and academic awards.
* Oversee the final J.D., ELL.M., LL.M., and J.S.D graduation clearance process and diploma audits.

### **Departmental Leadership \& Strategic Systems (15%)**


* Manage daily office operations, set departmental goals, and handle budget administration for the office.
* Manage, mentor, and evaluate a team of direct reports within Registration Services.
* Partner with CUIT and Law School IT to audit, modernize, and automate registration technologies (BORIS, LawNet, Vergil).
* Collaborate closely with Student Services, Financial Aid, J.D. and Graduate Program Admissions teams, and Career Services to support seamless student services.
* Serve on ex\-officio administrative and curriculum committees at request to evaluate policy feasibility and academic calendar development.

### **Departmental Support \& Other Duties (10%)**


* Lead cross\-office collaboration during high\-volume periods (registration, exams, orientation, and graduation).
* Perform other related duties as assigned by the Associate Dean to maintain institutional priorities.

Minimum Qualifications


* Bachelor’s degree required; Advanced degree (Master’s, J.D., or equivalent) strongly preferred.
* Minimum of 7 to 9 years of progressive management and supervisory experience in a higher education registrar’s office or academic administration environment (law school setting preferred).

Preferred Qualifications


* Demonstrated knowledge of Student Information Systems (SIS, Banner, or equivalent), registration allocation engines, exam management platforms (e.g., Exam4, ExamSoft), and reporting tools.
* Deep understanding of ABA accreditation requirements, state bar certification rules, and FERPA regulations.
* Exceptional attention to detail, strong oral and written communication skills, and a demonstrated ability to thrive in a high\-volume, fast\-paced environment while managing competing deadlines.
* Must be able to work with diverse constituencies and support an inclusive workplace environment.
* Some evening and weekend work is required during peak operational cycles, specifically during examination periods, add/drop cycles, and bar certification windows

Equal Opport

jobs.title: Development and Program Director
jobs.description:
**Development and Program Director**

**Position Type:** Full time, exempt. Part time may be considered for the right candidate.  
**Location:** Carbondale, Colorado office  
**Reports to:** Executive Director  
**Application Deadline:** October 15, 2026  
**Target Start Date:** November 10, 2026

We are seeking a dynamic and strategic Development and Program Director to lead our organization’s fundraising initiatives, program development, and community engagement efforts. This vital role combines visionary leadership with hands\-on management of donor relations, grant writing, and event planning. The ideal candidate will possess a passion for advancing our mission through innovative strategies, exceptional relationship management, and effective resource development. As a key member of our leadership team, you will drive growth by cultivating major gifts, managing comprehensive fundraising campaigns, and overseeing program implementation to maximize impact. This position offers an exciting opportunity to shape the future of our organization while fostering meaningful connections within the community.

**Make Every Week Count**

Every week looks different in this role, and that is the point. One day you are closing a grant that funds financial literacy for thousands of students. The next you are coordinating with a middle school teacher to promote the Civics Bee. If you love variety, thrive on relationships, and want your work to change young lives across the Roaring Fork Valley and Colorado, this role is for you.

Youthentity is seeking a dynamic Development and Program Director to grow our fundraising, lead our Financial Literacy programs, and build our new Regional Civics Bee. This senior leadership role blends donor relations, grant writing, program management, and team leadership, all in service of helping young people become Money Smart and Career Ready.

**Why This Role Matters**

Last year, Youthentity reached over 8,200 students across 104 schools. Students in our financial literacy programs gain an average 33% increase in financial knowledge, and our Career Academies achieve 100% certification rates. As Development and Program Director, you will fuel that impact and help us reach even more students statewide.

**What You Will Do**

**Development and Fundraising**

* Shape and lead a comprehensive fundraising strategy for corporate, foundation, and individual giving, in partnership with the Executive Director.
* Develop and manage the annual fundraising plan, calendar, and budget, including annual campaigns, year\-end appeals, and Colorado Gives Day.
* Grow the major gifts program by researching, cultivating, and stewarding a portfolio of donors.
* Build corporate partnerships and event sponsorships.
* Research, write, and submit new and renewal grant applications and reports on time and with accuracy.
* Help lead signature events, including the Annual Pig Roast.
* Support board members in their fundraising roles and staff the development committee.
* Oversee donor acknowledgment and appreciation so every supporter feels the impact of their gift.
* Gather student stories, photos, and short videos to power donor communications, social media, and impact reports.
* Maintain accurate development records in Neon CRM and report fundraising results to the Executive Director and board.

**Program Leadership and Management**

* Lead and actively engage in the Financial Literacy and Civics Bee programs.
* Lead a team of two to four remote staff from our Carbondale office.
* Grow the Greater Roaring Fork Valley Regional Civics Bee, including program coordination, school and family outreach, and event execution.
* Measure program outcomes and turn data into compelling, grant ready impact reports.
* Manage student and program data in our CRM system.

**Team Player**

Youthentity runs on a small, highly collaborative staff. You will support other programs and events as needed, and your colleagues will do the same for you. This description outlines core responsibilities but does not include every possible duty. Management may update it as needs evolve.

**You Will Thrive Here If**

* You get energy from switching gears and no two days feel the same.
* You see fundraising as relationship building, not transactions.
* You love building something new and watching it grow.
* You are passionate about serving the youth in our community.
* You roll up your sleeves when a teammate needs a hand.

**Qualifications**

**Required**

* Six or more years of relevant professional experience
* Proven experience in development, fundraising, and donor relations best practices
* Grant writing experience with a track record of success
* Strong leadership and team management experience
* Exceptional written and verbal communication skills
* Event planning and execution experience
* Familiarity with nonprofit development and communications
* Experience working with youth and educational programs
* Proficiency with Neon CRM, Mailchimp, Canva, Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, and Microsoft Office
* Highly organized, detail oriented, and able to juggle multiple priorities in a fast\-paced environment
* Availability for occasional evenings and weekends for programs and events

**Preferred**

* Basic video editing skills

**Work Environment and Schedule**

* Based in our Carbondale, Colorado office
* Monday through Friday schedule for full time; part time schedule may be discussed
* Occasional evenings and weekends for events and programs
* Occasional regional travel
* Some weeks may exceed 40 hours during peak events and deadlines

**Compensation and Benefits**

* Salary: $68,000 to $90,000, commensurate with experience
* 7 paid holidays and 4 weeks paid time off
* Medical, dental, and vision insurance
* 401(k) plan with company match
* HSA with company contribution

**Life at Youthentity**

Join a small, passionate team that celebrates wins together. Enjoy community events and the occasional treat from our student run bu

jobs.title: Branch Executive Director
jobs.description:
Description:  

The Branch Executive Director provides strategic and operational leadership for an assigned YMCA branch, ensuring excellence in member experience, program quality, financial performance, community impact, and staff development. Reporting to the President \& CEO, this leader is responsible for the overall management of branch operations, including membership growth, program development, fundraising, fiscal stewardship, board and volunteer engagement, and community partnerships. The Executive Director advances the YMCA's mission through Cause\-Driven Leadership and a culture of inclusion, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

**1\. Branch Leadership \& Operations**

* Provide overall leadership and management of day\-to\-day branch operations.
* Ensure high\-quality, safe, and mission\-driven programs, services, and facilities.
* Oversee membership engagement, retention, and growth through exceptional customer service and innovative programming.
* Ensure compliance with YMCA policies, risk management standards, and operational procedures.

**2\. Financial Management**

* Develop, manage, and achieve annual operating and capital budgets.
* Monitor financial performance through forecasting, variance analysis, expense management, and revenue growth strategies.
* Ensure sound financial controls and compliance with Association accounting policies.
* Manage reserve accounts and long\-term financial planning.

**3\. Fundraising \& Community Engagement**

* Lead the branch's Annual Giving Campaign and other fundraising initiatives to meet financial development goals.
* Cultivate relationships with donors, community leaders, businesses, foundations, and government partners.
* Represent the YMCA throughout the community while strengthening strategic partnerships and public awareness.

**4\. Staff \& Volunteer Leadership**

* Recruit, develop, supervise, and retain high\-performing staff and volunteers.
* Foster a positive, inclusive workplace culture focused on accountability, professional development, and organizational excellence.
* Conduct performance evaluations, succession planning, and staff development initiatives.

**5\. Board Development \& Governance**

* Partner with the Branch Board of Managers and its committees to advance strategic priorities.
* Support board recruitment, orientation, engagement, and committee effectiveness.
* Provide leadership for strategic planning and annual operational planning.

**6\. Program \& Membership Development**

* Lead the development, evaluation, and continuous improvement of YMCA programs and services.
* Drive membership recruitment, retention, and engagement strategies.
* Expand programs in alignment with community needs and Association priorities.

**7\. Leadership Priorities**

* Provide exceptional leadership for all branch operations.
* Achieve financial, membership, and program performance goals.
* Build strong staff, volunteer, and board leadership.
* Strengthen community partnerships and philanthropic support.
* Foster innovation, operational excellence, and an outstanding member experience.


Requirements:
* Bachelor's degree in Business, Human Services, Recreation, Nonprofit Management, or a related field preferred.
* Five or more years of progressive leadership experience in YMCA, nonprofit, health and wellness, recreation, or comparable business operations.
* Demonstrated success in financial management, fundraising, strategic planning, staff leadership, and operational management.
* Proven ability to develop community partnerships and lead volunteer boards.
* Strong communication, relationship\-building, and decision\-making skills.
* YMCA Multi\-Team Leader Certification preferred or the ability to obtain.
* Ability to respond to operational emergencies and maintain an on\-site leadership presence, including occasional evenings and weekends.

**WORK ENVIRONMENT:**


This position requires regular on\-site leadership in a dynamic facility environment, including offices, wellness areas, aquatics, youth program spaces, and outdoor locations. The role requires the ability to manage multiple priorities, lift up to 50 pounds, and respond to operational needs as required.

jobs.title: Chase Home Lending, Executive Director Strategic Initiatives PMO & Workforce Agility Program Director
jobs.description:
**JOB DESCRIPTION**  

  

  

The future of work is being built right now — and you could be the one leading it. At JPMorganChase, we are investing boldly in transforming how our people work, how teams are organized, and how technology and human capabilities come together to deliver for our customers. This is your opportunity to shape that future at one of the world's most influential financial institutions.


As a **Strategic Initiatives PMO and Workforce Agility Program Director** within Chase Home Lending, you will lead the firm's most consequential workforce transformation efforts across all Home Lending business teams while **overseeing the Strategic Initiatives PMO** that drives planning, execution, integration and adoption of high\-impact strategic initiatives. You will establish scalable program infrastructure, provide centralized oversight across initiatives, and ensure measurable outcomes through strong governance, disciplined execution, and stakeholder alignment. You will directly influence how work is structured, how AI, automation and emerging technologies reshape work, organizational structures, and customer experiences, and how our teams are positioned to perform at their best. This is a high\-visibility leadership role that sits at the intersection of strategy, operations, people, and technology — and your work will have a direct impact on the organization's performance and bottom line.


**Job responsibilities**


* Lead multiple cross\-organizational programs across Home Lending, driving workforce agility and transformation from ideation through execution and delivering measurable business results.
* Partner with senior business leaders and executive stakeholders to align workforce agility priorities with Home Lending's long\-term strategy and financial objectives.
* Lead workforce impact assessments to identify role, capacity, skill, organizational, and leadership implications associated with transformation initiatives.
* Partner with HR, Employee Readiness, Communications, and business teams to coordinate workforce readiness strategies that enable successful adoption of future\-state operating models.
* Own the Strategic Initiatives PMO portfolio across Home Lending, providing a centralized hub for program oversight, coordination, and support.
* Establish and maintain an integrated view across strategic initiatives, including plans, timelines, dependencies, deliverables, and risks, using consistent program management methodologies.
* Drive planning and execution of complex strategic initiatives, managing scope, schedule, budget, resources, risks, and deliverables aligned to business and customer needs.
* Serve as a strategic thought partner to business leaders, translating complex operational challenges into structured and executable programs.
* Manage and develop program staff, fostering a high\-performing, inclusive, and collaborative team culture.
* Monitor program health, progress, and risks, proactively addressing issues, resolving conflicts, and adjusting priorities to maintain execution momentum.
* Manage program budgets, track spend against plan, and optimize resource allocation to maximize business outcomes

**Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills**


* Formal training or certification on program management concepts and 10\+ years applied experience
* Demonstrated experience leading large\-scale, cross\-organizational programs with significant financial, reputational, or operational impact
* Proven ability to manage and influence senior stakeholders, including executive leadership, across matrixed business environments
* Strong conflict resolution, change management, and decision\-making skills with the ability to navigate complex tradeoffs and competing priorities
* Experience managing program budgets, resource planning, and capacity management across multi\-disciplinary teams
* Ability to develop and articulate a well\-structured business case, including financial and bottom\-line impact analysis
* Track record of building cohesive, high\-performing teams through strong communication, coaching, and inclusive leadership
* Deep understanding of business process, operational risk, and controls with the ability to drive a risk and compliance agenda

**Preferred qualifications, capabilities, and skills**


* Experience leading workforce transformation, agility, or future\-of\-work programs within a large financial services or regulated industry environment
* Familiarity with AI\-enabled workflow design, intelligent automation, or workforce productivity technologies
* Knowledge of agile delivery frameworks (e.g., SAFe, Scrum, Kanban) applied in business or operations contexts
* Experience operating as a subject matter expert and trusted advisor to senior business leaders across multiple functions
* Advanced degree in Business Administration, Organizational Development, Operations Management, or a related field

Chase is a leading financial services firm, helping nearly half of America's households and small businesses achieve their financial goals through a broad range of financial products. Our mission is to create engaged, lifelong relationships and put our customers at the heart of everything we do. jobs.description:
Overview:

The Sr. Director of Major Gifts leads the Central Health Foundation’s major\-gifts function and develops and executes strategies to generate significant philanthropic support for Central Health’s mission, strategic priorities, and community impact. Reporting to the Foundation Chief Executive Officer, the Sr. Director manages a portfolio of qualified major\-gift prospects and donors through identification, qualification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship. The Sr. Director personally solicits significant philanthropic gifts and partners closely with the Foundation CEO on transformational and selected major\-gift opportunities requiring executive involvement. The position establishes disciplined prospect\- and moves\-management practices, develops individualized donor strategies, prepares compelling proposals, and maintains reliable pipeline and revenue forecasts. The Sr. Director leads the execution of the major\-gifts strategy and supports campaign implementation in partnership with Foundation Strategy, which retains responsibility for overarching campaign architecture, strategic prioritization, and organizational readiness. The Sr. Director also works closely with Grants, Annual Giving, Donor Stewardship, Communications, Foundation Operations, Central Health leaders, clinicians, Board members, and community partners to coordinate fundraising activity and donor engagement. The Sr. Director builds and leads the major\-gifts team as approved staffing plans develop. The position may initially operate as a senior individual contributor and player\-coach but is accountable for establishing the structure, practices, performance expectations, and team capacity needed to support a mature major\-gifts program.  

This is a hybrid position. Individuals in this position may work both at an approved off\-site location and onsite at a primary location or multiple locations based on business needs.

* Personally solicit assigned major\-gift prospects and participate in transformational and principal\-gift solicitations with the Foundation CEO and other designated leaders.
* Conduct or coordinate research, donor strategy, relationship mapping, and next\-step planning for CEO\-led and executive\-led relationships.
* Prepare the Foundation CEO, Board members, Central Health executives, clinicians, and community leaders for donor meetings and solicitations.
* Develop briefing materials, talking points, proposals, presentations, solicitation strategies, and follow\-up plans for significant gift opportunities.
* Coordinate the participation of executives, Board members, clinicians, volunteers, and other relationship partners in donor engagement.
* Clarify relationship ownership, solicitation roles, decision points, timelines, and follow\-up responsibilities.
* Track commitments and next steps associated with transformational, principal, and major\-gift strategies.

* Partner with Foundation Strategy, which leads overarching campaign architecture, funding themes, initiative sequencing, readiness requirements, and strategic prioritization.
* Provide donor\-market, portfolio, and pipeline insight to inform campaign priorities, feasibility, leadership engagement, solicitation planning, and fundraising goals.
* Participate substantially in prospect strategy and solicitation planning.
* Assess campaign readiness from a fundraising perspective, including prospect strength, donor interest, volunteer leadership, case development, and stewardship capacity.
* Develop or coordinate cases for support, donor proposals, initiative summaries, presentations, and solicitation materials.

new_jobs.title: CEO
new_jobs.description:
**Chief Executive Officer (CEO)**

**The Joy Culture Foundation (TJCF)** \| Menlo Park, CA \| Hybrid

The CEO is TJCF’s chief ambassador and executive leader, responsible for mission delivery, organizational health, strategic growth, and sustained community impact. In partnership with the Board, the CEO sets vision and priorities, leads a small high\-performing team (staff and volunteers), stewards major donor and partner relationships, and ensures excellent programming and library services.

**Key Responsibilities1\) Strategy \& Mission Delivery**

● Lead multi\-year strategic planning and annual operating plans that align programs and community needs while ensuring long\-term financial sustainability and legal compliance

● Deliver high\-quality and meaningful programs that advance TJCF’s vision and create lasting community impact

● Translate strategy into measurable goals, budgets, timelines, and outcomes

**2\) Organizational Leadership**

● Hire, coach, motivate, and retain a small, mission\-aligned team, including core staff, teachers, and librarians

● Champion a culture of community, kindness and teamwork

● Develop volunteer leadership pipelines; recognize and grow community champions

**3\) Board Governance** 

● Partner closely with the Board on strategy, policy, and performance; prepare timely reports and materials; run quarterly board meetings

● Support Board development: recruitment, onboarding, committee engagement, and effective meetings.

**2\) Fundraising \& Donor Relations**

● Own annual contributed\-revenue goals across major gifts, grants, events, corporate sponsorships, and community giving

● Build and manage a robust major donor pipeline; personally cultivate, solicit, and steward top prospects

● Serve as primary spokesperson; strengthen brand, marketing, and media presence

● Build partnerships with schools, libraries, civic organizations, cultural groups, and sponsors

**Qualifications**

● 10\+ years of progressive leadership in nonprofits, education, libraries, museums, community development, or startups

● Deep commitment to advancing TJCF’s mission and vision

● Inspiring leader, communicator and relationship builder

● Builder of teams, systems, and culture in resource\-conscious environments

● Strategic thinker who executes with discipline and clarity

● Strong financial acumen

● Adaptable, hands\-on, and calm under pressure—comfortable switching between high\-level strategy and day\-to\-day operations

● Bilingual Mandarin/English

● Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree a plus (MA, MPA, MBA, MLIS, or related).

**About TJCF**

The Joy Culture Foundation (TJCF) is a community\-driven nonprofit dedicated to family learning and bilingual cultural enrichment. We operate the **Little Bookworm Chinese Library** in Menlo Park and host high\-impact community programs such as the **Little Entrepreneur Fair**, seasonal cultural family days (CNY/Dragon Boat/Mid\-Autumn), reading challenges, weekend classes, and youth leadership initiatives. Our vision is a welcoming, bilingual hub where families learn, connect, and thrive.

**How to apply** 

Email CV to lulu.roberts@thejoyculturefoundation.org

Pay: From $80,000\.00 per year

Benefits:

* Flexible schedule

Work Location: Hybrid remote in Menlo Park, CA 94025

new_jobs.title: Development and Program Director
new_jobs.description:
**Development and Program Director**

**Position Type:** Full time, exempt. Part time may be considered for the right candidate.  
**Location:** Carbondale, Colorado office  
**Reports to:** Executive Director  
**Application Deadline:** October 15, 2026  
**Target Start Date:** November 10, 2026

We are seeking a dynamic and strategic Development and Program Director to lead our organization’s fundraising initiatives, program development, and community engagement efforts. This vital role combines visionary leadership with hands\-on management of donor relations, grant writing, and event planning. The ideal candidate will possess a passion for advancing our mission through innovative strategies, exceptional relationship management, and effective resource development. As a key member of our leadership team, you will drive growth by cultivating major gifts, managing comprehensive fundraising campaigns, and overseeing program implementation to maximize impact. This position offers an exciting opportunity to shape the future of our organization while fostering meaningful connections within the community.

**Make Every Week Count**

Every week looks different in this role, and that is the point. One day you are closing a grant that funds financial literacy for thousands of students. The next you are coordinating with a middle school teacher to promote the Civics Bee. If you love variety, thrive on relationships, and want your work to change young lives across the Roaring Fork Valley and Colorado, this role is for you.

Youthentity is seeking a dynamic Development and Program Director to grow our fundraising, lead our Financial Literacy programs, and build our new Regional Civics Bee. This senior leadership role blends donor relations, grant writing, program management, and team leadership, all in service of helping young people become Money Smart and Career Ready.

**Why This Role Matters**

Last year, Youthentity reached over 8,200 students across 104 schools. Students in our financial literacy programs gain an average 33% increase in financial knowledge, and our Career Academies achieve 100% certification rates. As Development and Program Director, you will fuel that impact and help us reach even more students statewide.

**What You Will Do**

**Development and Fundraising**

* Shape and lead a comprehensive fundraising strategy for corporate, foundation, and individual giving, in partnership with the Executive Director.
* Develop and manage the annual fundraising plan, calendar, and budget, including annual campaigns, year\-end appeals, and Colorado Gives Day.
* Grow the major gifts program by researching, cultivating, and stewarding a portfolio of donors.
* Build corporate partnerships and event sponsorships.
* Research, write, and submit new and renewal grant applications and reports on time and with accuracy.
* Help lead signature events, including the Annual Pig Roast.
* Support board members in their fundraising roles and staff the development committee.
* Oversee donor acknowledgment and appreciation so every supporter feels the impact of their gift.
* Gather student stories, photos, and short videos to power donor communications, social media, and impact reports.
* Maintain accurate development records in Neon CRM and report fundraising results to the Executive Director and board.

**Program Leadership and Management**

* Lead and actively engage in the Financial Literacy and Civics Bee programs.
* Lead a team of two to four remote staff from our Carbondale office.
* Grow the Greater Roaring Fork Valley Regional Civics Bee, including program coordination, school and family outreach, and event execution.
* Measure program outcomes and turn data into compelling, grant ready impact reports.
* Manage student and program data in our CRM system.

**Team Player**

Youthentity runs on a small, highly collaborative staff. You will support other programs and events as needed, and your colleagues will do the same for you. This description outlines core responsibilities but does not include every possible duty. Management may update it as needs evolve.

**You Will Thrive Here If**

* You get energy from switching gears and no two days feel the same.
* You see fundraising as relationship building, not transactions.
* You love building something new and watching it grow.
* You are passionate about serving the youth in our community.
* You roll up your sleeves when a teammate needs a hand.

**Qualifications**

**Required**

* Six or more years of relevant professional experience
* Proven experience in development, fundraising, and donor relations best practices
* Grant writing experience with a track record of success
* Strong leadership and team management experience
* Exceptional written and verbal communication skills
* Event planning and execution experience
* Familiarity with nonprofit development and communications
* Experience working with youth and educational programs
* Proficiency with Neon CRM, Mailchimp, Canva, Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, and Microsoft Office
* Highly organized, detail oriented, and able to juggle multiple priorities in a fast\-paced environment
* Availability for occasional evenings and weekends for programs and events

**Preferred**

* Basic video editing skills

**Work Environment and Schedule**

* Based in our Carbondale, Colorado office
* Monday through Friday schedule for full time; part time schedule may be discussed
* Occasional evenings and weekends for events and programs
* Occasional regional travel
* Some weeks may exceed 40 hours during peak events and deadlines

**Compensation and Benefits**

* Salary: $68,000 to $90,000, commensurate with experience
* 7 paid holidays and 4 weeks paid time off
* Medical, dental, and vision insurance
* 401(k) plan with company match
* HSA with company contribution

**Life at Youthentity**

Join a small, passionate team that celebrates wins together. Enjoy community events and the occasional treat from our student run bu
